api: repair_line_chunk(session_id, line_id, chunk_no, payload, expected_line_version, expected_chunk_version)
identifiers: Canonical mathematical and document IDs are meaningful lowercase snake_case text. UUIDs and bare numeric sequence IDs are not permitted.
Generated mathematical ID collisions use alphabetic suffixes (_b, _c, ..., _z, _aa, ...) rather than numeric suffixes.

Session IDs are the operational exception: session_<project>_r<global_revision>_<sequence>. The revision records the database state at startup; the final sequence only distinguishes concurrent or repeated boots at that same revision.
Chore IDs exposed to workers are meaningful snake_case text. Internal numeric primary keys are implementation details.
Event ordering is exposed as a revision number, not an ID.
publication: Every substantive durable research publication must explicitly include dependencies, using [] when genuinely self-contained.
The declared dependency list replaces the consumer's prior premise set and records the actual premises of the new math version.
Brainstorm promotion likewise requires an explicit dependencies array.
When a result clearly changes a Main Line synthesis, include that Main Line update in the same staged publication batch.
reading: read() is the exact manuscript-content path and is statelessly paged.
Each call returns at most 9000 content characters plus compact metadata.
Pass next_cursor back to read() until complete=true.
context(), search(), and brainstorms() are navigation surfaces and do not substitute for exact paged reads.
research_lines: Research Lines are assembled manuscripts authored as ordered subsection-sized chunks.
Ordinary development edits only the hot chunk with save_line_chunk().
repair_line_chunk() is the exceptional version-guarded path for correcting an older crystallized chunk in place; the chunk remains crystallized.
Substantive hot-chunk edits and crystallized-chunk repairs both bump the line math_version and require explicit dependencies.
Crystallization freezes the hot chunk and opens a new empty hot chunk without changing the line math_version.
searching: search() matches titles, simplified statements, statements, and full bodies; documents are included by default.
Results are ordered primarily by literal match count per object, then full-text relevance, title, and id.
filters.result_level may be ids, metadata, simplified, statement, or full; simplified is the default.
Each call returns one packed result page capped at 9000 characters. filters.offset is the number of complete packed pages to skip.
A result that would cross a page boundary moves intact to the next page; only a result larger than an empty page is truncated.
startup: boot() returns startup_notices from startup_steward(), including empty-Brainstorm and stale Main Line warnings.

After choosing a route, one route-specific search across existing Research Lines and Toolkit entries is strongly recommended to avoid rediscovery, but it is never a gate and proof work must not be blocked if it is skipped.
Then perform the narrow changes()/read() freshness check for the chosen Main Line and Research Line.
usage: Call through the active project schema. boot() returns a human-readable session_id such as session_gn3n_r742_1; use that text ID for all later mutations.
